mainTopic: Who is deferred to פסח שני (טמא שרץ, דרך רחוקה), and the refutations of רבא's measurements of the twilight walk and of the size of the world.
overview: This amud opens by settling an earlier difficulty. According to רב יהודה, a טמא שרץ is pushed off to פסח שני because the Torah's verse itself defers an impure person, even one who could be pure by nightfall. Next, a ברייתא teaches that being on a דרך רחוקה depends on where you stand, beyond or inside מודיעים, and not on whether you can actually reach ירושלים. רבא then says the world is 6,000 פרסאות and the רקיע is 1,000 פרסאות thick, basing the second figure on רבי יוחנן's teaching about how far a person walks in a day. A ברייתא of רבי יהודה shows that dawn and dusk are only 4 מילין each, which refutes רבא and עולא. רבי יוחנן is defended because he only gave the full-day total, and רבי חנינא is defended because the angels made לוט hurry. Then three sources refute רבא's 6,000-פרסה world size: the size of מצרים and כוש, רבי נתן's 'one star', and the sun crossing the inhabited world in one hour. A fourth challenge begins with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's story of the בת קול answering נבוכדנצר, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Torah itself defers the impure person
steps.stepSummary: According to רב יהודה, the difficulty about the טמא שרץ is resolved. The Torah explicitly defers an impure person to פסח שני even when he could be pure by nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב יהודה there is no difficulty. The Torah deferred the one who is impure from a שרץ, as it is written: 'Any man who shall be impure due to a dead body.' Are we not dealing even with a case where his seventh day falls on ערב פסח? Even so, the Torah said: let him be deferred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a difficulty raised earlier. It explains why, according to רב יהודה, a טמא שרץ still goes to פסח שני even though he can become pure in time to eat that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was this: if a person counts as 'able' to bring the פסח when he can be fit by the evening meal, a טמא שרץ should also count as able. He can immerse during the day and be pure at nightfall. The answer is that this case is not decided by logic but by a verse. The Torah defers a טמא מת even on his seventh day, when he too could be pure by night. That shows that anyone impure at the time of the שחיטה is deferred.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone made impure by touching a dead creeping creature. He becomes pure after immersion and nightfall.
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
Pushed him off (to פסח שני)
'Are we not dealing with…?' This introduces a case the verse must also include.
The day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the טמא שרץ is deferred because he truly cannot eat that night. He could be pure by nightfall. He is deferred only because the Torah's verse says so.

phrases.english: According to Rav Yehuda it is not difficult:
one impure from a creeping animal, the Torah deferred him,
as it is written:
"Any man who shall be impure due to a dead body,"
are we not dealing (even with a case)
phrases.notes: He's asking this to make a point: surely the verse covers this case too.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחָל שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: where his seventh day happens to fall on Pesach eve,
and even so the Torah said: let him be deferred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised in the previous section, on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural decree: the verse itself defers an impure person, so logic about being able to eat in time does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טמא שרץ who can be pure by nightfall should be treated as able to bring the פסח, just like someone who can arrive in time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah defers anyone impure at the time of שחיטה, as shown by the טמא מת on his seventh day.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two different reasons a person goes to פסח שני: being on a journey, which depends on measurement, and being impure, which is a fixed rule from the verse.

steps.title: Beyond מודיעים but able to arrive by riding
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone standing beyond מודיעים is on a דרך רחוקה and is exempt, even if he could reach ירושלים on horses or mules.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he was standing outside מודיעים and could enter (ירושלים) with horses and mules, I might think he is liable. The verse teaches: 'and was not on a journey.' This one was on a journey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines a 'distant journey' by where the person stands. His actual ability to get there does not change it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that if he can reach ירושלים in time by riding, he is obligated and gets כרת for not coming. The verse says the punishment applies only to one who 'was not on a journey.' Since this man is beyond מודיעים, he is by definition on a journey, so he is exempt even though riding could get him there.

keyTerms.meaning: A town that marks the boundary of a 'distant journey' from ירושלים
'I might have thought…'. This sets up a mistaken assumption.
'The verse teaches'. This introduces the verse that corrects the assumption.
'And was not on a journey' (במדבר ט:יג)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
if he was standing outside (beyond) Modi'im,
and was able to enter (Jerusalem) on horses and mules,
I might think he is liable —
therefore the verse says: "and was not on a journey,"
and this one was on a journey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new ברייתא that defines דרך רחוקה by location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone beyond מודיעים is on a דרך רחוקה and is exempt, even if he could arrive by riding.

steps.title: Inside מודיעים but delayed by traffic
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ברייתא: someone inside the מודיעים boundary is not on a journey. He is liable even if camels and wagons hold him up.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was standing inside מודיעים and could not enter because camels and wagons were delaying him, I might think he is not liable. The verse teaches: 'and was not on a journey.' This one was not on a journey.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite case. Being close to ירושלים makes a person obligated, even if something practical slows him down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together the two cases show the rule clearly. The location of the person decides, not his actual ability to arrive. He could have left the slow caravan and walked in, so the delay does not exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside (closer than) מודיעים
Camels and wagons
That delay or hold back

steps.whatToRemember: דרך רחוקה is set by where you stand. Beyond מודיעים you are exempt even if you could ride in. Inside מודיעים you are liable even if you are delayed.

phrases.english: if he was standing inside (closer than) Modi'im,
and was not able to enter
because of camels and wagons that were delaying him,
I might think he is not liable —
therefore the verse says: "and was not on a journey,"
and this one was not on a journey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror case that completes the ברייתא begun in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone inside מודיעים is not on a journey and is liable, even if outside obstacles delay him.

steps.title: The size of the world and the thickness of the sky
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives two measurements: the world is 6000 פרסאות and the רקיע is 1000 פרסאות thick. One is from tradition and one is from reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The world is six thousand פרסאות, and the thickness of the רקיע is one thousand פרסאות. One of these is a tradition and one is reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's measurements. They set up the next move: supporting the assumption about how far a person walks between dawn and sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ratio of world to רקיע is 6 to 1. The walking day is likewise divided, with the stretch from dawn to sunrise being one-sixth of the walk across the 'world' of the day. This lets the גמרא check the figure of five מיל before sunrise. רבא admits that only one number is a received tradition and the other is his own logic.

keyTerms.meaning: Parasang, a unit of distance (4 מיל)
The world
The thickness of the sky or firmament
Here it means a received tradition
Reasoning or logic

steps.confusionAlert: Here גמרא does not mean 'the Talmud'. It means a teaching received by tradition, as opposed to סברא, one's own reasoning.

phrases.english: Rava said:
the world is six thousand parasangs,
and the thickness of the firmament is one thousand parasangs.
One is a tradition, and one is reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שִׁיתָּא אַלְפֵי פַּרְסֵי הָוֵי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to cosmological measurements that will support the earlier walking-distance calculation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world is 6000 פרסאות and the רקיע is 1000 פרסאות thick, a 6 to 1 ratio. One figure is tradition and the other is reasoning.

steps.title: רבא's reasoning is built on רבי יוחנן's walking distances
steps.stepSummary: רבא's 1000-פרסאות figure comes from רבי יוחנן's teaching that a person walks 40 מילין a day, with 5 מילין in each twilight period. The twilight is therefore one-sixth of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא holds like what רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן. An average person walks ten פרסאות (40 מילין) in a day. From dawn until sunrise he walks five מילין, and from sunset until the stars come out he walks five מילין. So the thickness of the רקיע is one-sixth of the day's travel.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 4, רבא said one of his measurements came from reasoning. Here the גמרא explains that reasoning: it is a calculation based on רבי יוחנן's walking distances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full day is 40 מילין. Take away 5 for dawn and 5 for dusk, and 30 מילין are left for sunrise to sunset. The sun is crossing the thickness of the רקיע during dawn, so that crossing equals 5 out of 30, which is one-sixth. One-sixth of 6000 פרסאות is 1000 פרסאות.

keyTerms.meaning: A parasang, a unit of distance equal to 4 מילין
A unit of distance, about 2000 אמות
Dawn, when the first light appears
Sunrise, when the sun itself appears
Nightfall, when the stars come out
The thickness of the sky/firmament

steps.confusionAlert: The 'one-sixth' is measured against the sunrise-to-sunset part of the day (30 מילין), not against the full 40 מילין.

phrases.english: He (רבא) holds like this
that Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
How far does an average person walk in a day?
Ten parasangs (40 mil).
From dawn until sunrise
five mil,
from sunset until the stars come out
five mil,
it turns out the thickness of the firmament is
one-sixth of the day.
phrases.notes: That's 5 of the 30 מילין between sunrise and sunset, which works out to 1000 of the 6000 פרסאות.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning-based source behind רבא's measurement in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Average walk is 40 מילין a day, with 5 in each twilight period, so the רקיע is one-sixth of the day's travel (1000 פרסאות).

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the firmament is only one-tenth of the day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה, who says each twilight period is only 4 מילין. That makes the רקיע one-tenth of the day, not one-sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects from a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says the thickness of the רקיע is one-tenth of the day. Proof: an average person walks ten פרסאות a day. From dawn to sunrise he walks four מילין, and from sunset to the stars four מילין. So the רקיע is one-tenth of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה uses the same 40-מילין day but assigns only 4 מילין to each twilight period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the full day is 40 מילין. They disagree about the twilight: רבי יהודה says 4 מילין, while רבא's source says 5. Four out of the 40-מיל day is one-tenth, so the רקיע is much thinner than רבא's one-sixth.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that this is so), which introduces a proof
Four מילין

phrases.english: They objected: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹבְיוֹ שֶׁל רָקִיעַ אֶחָד מֵעֲשָׂרָה בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.english: The thickness of the firmament is one-tenth of the day.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע, כַּמָּה מַהֲלַךְ אָדָם בֵּינוֹנִי בַּיּוֹם —
phrases.english: Know this: how far does an average person walk in a day?
Ten parasangs,
and from dawn until sunrise
four mil,
from sunset until the stars come out
four mil,
it turns out the thickness of the firmament is
one-tenth of the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the twilight distance that step 5's calculation depends on
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's figure (via רבי יוחנן's 5-מיל twilight) that the רקיע is one-sixth of the day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא (תנאי-level source) gives 4 מילין for each twilight period, which produces a one-tenth ratio and contradicts רבא.

steps.title: A full refutation of רבא and עולא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא refutes רבא and also עולא, who both used the 5-מיל twilight. The refutation stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבא. It is also a refutation of עולא. It is a full refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge works. Both רבא and עולא built on the 5-מיל twilight, and the ברייתא disproves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא had earlier used 5 מילין for each twilight to say a person walks 15 מילין in half a day. רבי יהודה's 4-מיל figure contradicts both of them. Since a ברייתא outweighs אמוראים, the refutation is final.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a decisive disproof of an אמורא's view

steps.whatToRemember: The 5-מיל twilight figure is rejected. רבי יהודה's 4 מילין stands, which makes the רקיע one-tenth of the day.

phrases.english: A refutation of Rava,
a refutation of Ulla.
It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection of step 6 as decisive
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא and עולא are refuted, because each twilight period is 4 מילין and not 5.

steps.title: Is רבי יוחנן refuted too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן, the source רבא relied on, is also refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is also a refutation of רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the refutation also reaches רבי יוחנן, whose teaching was quoted as רבא's basis. This question sets up the defense that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's teaching was cited with the 5-מיל twilight numbers. If those numbers came from him, he would be refuted along with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it will be (a suggestion that may be rejected)

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rabbi Yochanan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the refutation of step 7 to רבא's source
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching quoted in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 5-מיל twilight numbers appeared inside רבי יוחנן's quoted teaching, so it seems he is refuted too.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן only gave the full-day total
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן only said 40 מילין for a whole day. The 5-מיל twilight numbers were a mistaken addition by the רבנן (עולא and רבא), who counted people who start before dawn or keep walking after dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could say to you: I only spoke about the total for the day. It was the רבנן who made a mistake, because they counted those who start early and those who walk into the dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. His own statement was just '10 פרסאות a day,' and that total fits רבי יהודה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 5-מיל figure came from עולא and רבא, not from רבי יוחנן. They saw people covering 5 מילין in twilight, but those people had set out before dawn or kept walking after nightfall. The true twilight distance is 4 מילין.

keyTerms.meaning: In the daytime, meaning the day as a whole
They made a mistake
Starting early (before dawn) and walking into the darkness

phrases.english: He could say to you:
I spoke only about the whole day,
and it is the Sages who erred,
because they counted those who set out early and those who walk into the dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא בִּימָמָא הוּא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by limiting what רבי יוחנן actually said
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source: the disputed detail belongs to later interpreters, not to the original speaker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 5-מיל twilight numbers were part of רבי יוחנן's own teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן only said 40 מילין per day. The twilight split was the רבנן's mistaken calculation.

steps.title: Is רבי חנינא refuted?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא proved that סדום to צוער is 5 מילין, because לוט walked it between dawn and sunrise. If that period is only 4 מילין, his proof seems to fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests another view that depends on a 5-מיל dawn period. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא learned from the פסוקים that לוט left סדום at dawn and reached צוער at sunrise, and that the distance is 5 מילין. Under רבי יהודה, dawn to sunrise is only 4 מילין, so the two seem to conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: The city לוט fled from and the town he escaped to

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rabbi Chanina?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same refutation to another 5-מיל-based view
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that סדום to צוער is 5 מילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוט walked that distance from dawn to sunrise, which רבי יהודה says is only 4 מילין of normal walking.

steps.title: The angels made לוט hurry
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'ויאיצו', meaning the angels rushed לוט. A hurried walk covers 5 מילין in the time it normally takes to walk 4.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'They hurried him' is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנינא. לוט was not walking at a normal pace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's 4 מילין is the pace of an average walker. The פסוק (וַיָּאִיצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים בְּלוֹט) shows the angels rushed him. So he covered 5 מילין in the dawn period, and both views can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And they hurried (him), the angels rushing לוט
It is different, a distinguishing answer

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: dawn and dusk are 4 מילין each at a normal pace. רבי יוחנן's 40-מיל day stands, and רבי חנינא's 5 מילין is explained by לוט's hurried pace.

phrases.english: No, 'and they hastened' is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by showing that לוט's case was an unusual pace
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the special speed in the פסוק explains the larger distance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוט walked at a normal pace, so the dawn period would have to be 5 מילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוט was rushed by the angels and covered 5 מילין in the normal 4-מיל period.

steps.title: מצרים, כוש, and the world: the measurements are far too big
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the size of מצרים (400 by 400 פרסאות). It says each place is 1/60 of the next: כוש, the world, גן, עדן, גיהנם. This makes the world much bigger than 6,000 פרסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: מצרים was 400 פרסאות by 400 פרסאות. מצרים is one-sixtieth of כוש. כוש is one-sixtieth of the world. The world is one-sixtieth of the גן. The גן is one-sixtieth of עדן. עדן is one-sixtieth of גיהנם. So the entire world is like a pot-lid compared to גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with real numbers to challenge the claim that the world is only 6,000 פרסאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצרים alone is 400 פרסאות across. כוש is 60 times bigger, and the world is 60 times bigger than כוש. That is clearly far more than 6,000 פרסאות, so the small world-size cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A distance measure, about 4 מילין
One-sixtieth
The lid of a pot, a small piece compared to the whole pot
The place where the wicked are punished

steps.confusionAlert: The גן and עדן and גיהנם part is extra. The challenge comes from the first numbers: מצרים, then כוש, then the world. Those numbers already make the world far bigger than 6,000 פרסאות.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Egypt was four hundred parasangs
by four hundred parasangs,
and Egypt is one-sixtieth of Cush,
and Cush is one-sixtieth of the world,
and the world is one-sixtieth of the Garden,
and the Garden is one-sixtieth of Eden,
and Eden is one-sixtieth of Gehenna,
it turns out that the entire world
phrases.notes: The conclusion the ברייתא draws from the chain of sixtieths.

phrases.english: is like a pot-lid compared to Gehenna.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִצְרַיִם הָיָה אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 4 and attacks רבא's other figure, the 6,000-פרסה size of the world.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (attributed to רבא) that the whole world is 6,000 פרסאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 400 פרסאות × 60 × 60 gives a world far larger than 6,000 פרסאות.

steps.title: The first challenge is a real refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the challenge from מצרים and כוש a full refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says there is no answer, so the 6,000-פרסה claim is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא means the challenge stands with no defense. The small world-size is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation. The challenge stands and there is no answer.

phrases.english: A refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 6,000-פרסה world-size is refuted by the measurements of מצרים and כוש.

steps.title: רבי נתן: all inhabited land sits under one star
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of אליהו quotes רבי נתן. He says all the inhabited world sits under just one star.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what was taught in the school of אליהו: רבי נתן says, the entire inhabited world sits under one star.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. רבי נתן says all inhabited land is under a single star.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are countless stars in the sky. If all inhabited land fits under just one of them, then the whole world must be huge. That cannot fit with a world of only 6,000 פרסאות. The proof for רבי נתן's claim comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school (בית מדרש) of אליהו
The inhabited, settled part of the world
A star

phrases.english: Come and hear, for the school of Eliyahu taught:
Rabbi Natan says:
The entire inhabited world
sits under one star.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent challenge against the same 6,000-פרסה claim.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the whole world is 6,000 פרסאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all inhabited land fits under just one of the countless stars, the whole world must be enormous.

steps.title: Proof: the star stays above you wherever you walk
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן proves his claim. Wherever you travel in the inhabited world, a star you look at seems to stay right opposite you.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true. A person fixes his eye on one star. If he walks east, it stays opposite him. In all four directions, it stays opposite him. This shows that the entire inhabited world sits under one star.
steps.whatsHappening: This step brings the proof for רבי נתן's statement from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can travel as far as you like in any direction, and the star never seems to move from above you. רבי נתן takes this to mean that all inhabited land is 'under' that one star. That is the basis of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that it is so): this introduces a proof
Opposite him, directly facing him
The four directions of the world
By inference, from this we learn

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָדָם נוֹתֵן עֵינוֹ בְּכוֹכָב אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Know this, for a person sets his eye on one star:
he goes east, and it stands opposite him;
to all four directions of the world, it stands opposite him.
By inference, the entire inhabited world
sits under one star.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָדָם נוֹתֵן עֵינוֹ בְּכוֹכָב אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim made in Step 14, which strengthens the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's claim that all inhabited land is under one star
steps.raayaSupportSource: What people see: a star stays opposite you no matter where you walk

steps.title: The second challenge is also a real refutation
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן's 'one star' source fully refutes the 6,000-פרסה claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that the second challenge also stands with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second source refutes the claim, just like the first. The small world-size is now rejected by two separate sources.

phrases.english: A refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Steps 14-15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'one star' source also refutes the 6,000-פרסה world-size.

steps.title: The inhabited world is only one hour of the sun's path
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the inhabited world lies between עגלה (north) and עקרב (south). It also says the inhabited world is only one hour's worth of the day, because the sun is over it for just one hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: עגלה is in the north and עקרב is in the south. The entire inhabited world sits only between עגלה and עקרב. The entire inhabited world is only one hour of the day, because the sun passes over the inhabited world for only one hour a day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge. It says the inhabited world is only a tiny slice of the whole world: one hour out of the sun's twelve-hour daily path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun is over the inhabited world for just one hour. That makes the inhabited world only about 1/12 of the whole world. The inhabited world alone is already very large, so the whole world must be far bigger than 6,000 פרסאות.

keyTerms.meaning: A star group (the Big Dipper) in the north
A star group (Scorpio) in the south
The sun
One hour of the day

phrases.english: Come and hear: Ursa Major is in the north,
and Scorpio is in the south,
and the entire inhabited world sits
only between Ursa Major and Scorpio.
And the entire inhabited world amounts to
only one hour of the day,
for the sun enters over the inhabited world
only one hour a day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עֲגָלָה בַּצָּפוֹן, וְעַקְרָב בַּדָּרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, independent challenge against the same 6,000-פרסה claim.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the whole world is 6,000 פרסאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The inhabited world is only 1/12 of the sun's daily path, so the whole world is about 12 times the inhabited world, which is far over 6,000 פרסאות.

steps.title: Proof: the sun is overhead for everyone in the same hour
steps.stepSummary: At hour 5 the sun is still in the east, and at hour 7 it is in the west. From the middle of hour 6 to the middle of hour 7, it is directly overhead for every person. So the sun crosses the inhabited world in one hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true. At the fifth hour the sun is in the east. At the seventh hour the sun is in the west. During the second half of the sixth hour and the first half of the seventh hour, the sun stands over every person's head.
steps.whatsHappening: This step brings the proof for the 'one hour' claim from Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone in the inhabited world sees the sun straight overhead during the same one-hour window. So the sun crosses all inhabited land in just one hour. For the rest of the day, it is over land where no one lives.

keyTerms.meaning: East
West
The second half of the sixth hour and the first half of the seventh hour (midday)
Over every person's head, directly overhead

steps.confusionAlert: 'Hours' here are counted from the start of the day. Hour 6 to hour 7 is midday.

phrases.english: Know this, for at the fifth hour the sun is in the east,
and at the seventh hour the sun is in the west;
during half the sixth and half the seventh hour
the sun stands over the head of every person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'one hour' claim of Step 17, which strengthens the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the sun is over the inhabited world for only one hour a day
steps.raayaSupportSource: What people see: the sun is overhead for everyone during the same midday hour

steps.title: The third challenge is also a real refutation
steps.stepSummary: The 'one hour' source also fully refutes the 6,000-פרסה claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that the third challenge also stands with no answer. The next step opens yet another challenge against the same claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three separate sources show that the world is much bigger than 6,000 פרסאות. They are the measurements, the one star, and the one hour. Each one ends in תיובתא, so the small world-size is completely rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: The world-size of 6,000 פרסאות is refuted three times: by the size of מצרים and כוש, by רבי נתן's 'one star', and by the sun crossing the inhabited world in one hour.

phrases.english: A refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Steps 17-18; a further challenge follows in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 6,000-פרסה world-size is refuted by a third independent source (the sun crossing the inhabited world in one hour).

steps.title: A new challenge from the story of the boastful wicked king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens another challenge with תא שמע. It quotes רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's teaching about the בת קול that answered נבוכדנצר when he boasted, 'I will ascend above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear another challenge. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: What answer did the בת קול give that wicked man when he said, 'I will go up above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to the 6,000-פרסה claim. It tells us the background of a story, and the measurements that make up the challenge will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three sources have already knocked down the 6,000-פרסה claim: the size of מצרים and כוש, רבי נתן's star, and the 'one hour' ברייתא. Now a fourth source begins. The wicked man's boast about climbing to heaven will lead to an answer that gives very large distances, far bigger than 6,000 פרסאות.

keyTerms.meaning: A heavenly voice
'That wicked man': here נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר
The heights of the clouds

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a separate אגדה with no connection to the sugya. The story is brought only for the distances the בת קול will list, which challenge the 6,000-פרסה claim.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said:
What response did the Divine Voice answer him
to that wicked man
at the time that he said:
'I will ascend above the heights of the clouds,
I will be like the Most High'?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth source against the 6,000-פרסה claim, after the מצרים/כוש, one-star, and 'one hour' sources in steps 12-19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the world measures 6,000 פרסאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בת קול's answer will give enormous cosmic distances that do not fit a world of only 6,000 פרסאות.

steps.title: The heavenly voice begins its answer
steps.stepSummary: The בת קול comes out and begins rebuking נבוכדנצר, calling him 'wicked man, son of a wicked man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said to him: Wicked man, son of a wicked man,
steps.whatsHappening: The בת קול starts its reply to נבוכדנצר's boast. The opening is an insult, and the words that carry the challenge, the measurements, come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before giving any numbers, the voice puts the boaster in his place by calling him wicked and the son of a wicked man. This opening frames what follows: the distances will show how impossible his plan to reach heaven really is.

keyTerms.meaning: Came out, emerged
Wicked man, son of a wicked man

phrases.english: A Divine Voice emerged and said to him:
Wicked man, son of a wicked man,
phrases.notes: The rebuke continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question asked in step 20.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The בת קול's reply to נבוכדנצר, quoted by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
